The buyer has 3 open invoices with Adlerhof Trade Credit (CL01), total open exposure of EUR 189,100, with the worst item 25 days past due; the open invoice INV001567 alone is EUR 86,900. The payment file is labelled "improving" — days-late fell from 46 and 55 days on the two oldest settled invoices to 10 days on the most recent — but that read rests on only three settled invoices and is contradicted by the live 25 DPD position. Separately, Trade Ledger reported on 2026-09-20 that workers at the Essen facility staged a protest over delayed wage payments, with union representatives warning of further action if dues are not cleared.

The score is 47.7, placing the buyer in the Watch band with a PD of 0.3767. The trace is 0.65 x 33.3 (payment, 25 DPD) + 0.35 x 74.3 (news) = 47.7, so the news component contributes 26.0 and payment 21.7. The adjudicator agreed with caveats: the article is correctly attributed to this buyer (right entity, right city, no parent routing) and a payroll protest is a legitimate severity-5 distress signal. The caveat is that the two inputs are not independent — delayed wages and a past-due payment describe the same strain — so 47.7 likely sits at the conservative end of what this evidence implies. Note also that 26.0 of the 47.7 rests on a single uncorroborated two-sentence article from one publication.

The recommendation is REDUCE on LIM0040 (Adlerhof Trade Credit): cut the current limit of EUR 430,000 to a revised limit of EUR 285,373. The cut takes the line to where expected loss meets the 25% appetite, with PD at 0.3767 against a target of 0.25. Expected loss falls from EUR 131,205 to EUR 87,075 and maximum liability does not bind. This matters because the line has not been reviewed since 2024-10-24 while open exposure stands at EUR 189,100, leaving undrawn headroom available to a buyer now showing both payroll distress and a past-due position — the stale limit is not captured anywhere in the score and should be refreshed independently of the band.

Two things would lift this. First, clearing the 25 DPD item and evidence that the payroll arrears at Essen have actually been settled: the news component decays with age (base 75.0, already decayed to 74.29 at 5 days), so the buyer will drift back toward Healthy automatically even if the wage arrears are never cleared. Treat silence as unresolved and run an active re-check of payroll status rather than letting the score decay. Second, a refreshed credit line review plus more settled-invoice history — three settled invoices limit confidence in the "improving" trend, and corroboration of the Trade Ledger report from a second source would firm up the largest single input to the score.
